title: Two additions in a probabilistic program
statement:
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ natural-number registers, state set $\Lambda$, and oracle, and fix an input $x$ and register bound $B$. Let $k,y,p$ be register indices with $k
e y$, $k
e p$, and $p
e y$. Suppose the instruction at $test$ compares registers $k$ and $y$, going to $ex$ when they are equal and to $i_1$ otherwise; $i_1,i_2,i_3$ successively increment register $p$, with $i_3$ also incrementing $k$ and returning to $test$. For any rational $q$ and register valuation $v$ bounded by $B$, assume $v(k)\le v(y)$ and $v(p)+2(v(y)-v(k))\le B$. If, for the configuration at $ex$ with register $p$ increased by $2(v(y)-v(k))$ and register $k$ set to $v(y)$, the probabilistic semantics has acceptance probability $q$, then the configuration at $test$ with valuation $v$ has the same semantics and acceptance probability.
hypotheses_covered: The program $A$, oracle, input $x$, and bound $B$ are fixed
Every register value of $v$ is at most $B$
The specified configuration at $ex$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$ under bound $B$
